before.season: Dec-Apr (documented snowshoe/scramble ascents); summer conditions unconfirmed

July.reason: Early in the dry-season window; lingering snow or wet brush possible at lower elevations, and route-finding through the south-facing bands may be complicated by residual snow patches

August.reason: Peak dry-season conditions with heather and rock bands clear, matching the best-season window

September.reason: Still within the season but shorter days and higher chance of early-season weather changes in the Cascades

weather.typical: A Jul-Sep dry-season scramble in the Index/US-2 corridor
weather.probability: Cascade summer afternoon convection is a general regional pattern worth checking forecasts for

seasonal_hazards.exposure: Moderate fall exposure: there is route-finding through cliff bands and loose rock, so a slip near the cliff bands or on loose sections could result in a serious fall; staying on heather/easy rock and avoiding the steeper cliffs to either side is the key mitigation

avalanche.zone: Applies in season - this route is commonly climbed/approached on snow in winter and spring (the preferred strategy to avoid brutal summer brush), placing it within NWAC's active forecast window; check the NWAC Stevens Pass zone forecast before crossing the approach basin and PCT avalanche chutes.

crowds.peakTraffic: rarely climbed; if any traffic occurs it would be clear-weather summer weekends (Jul-Sep)
crowds.estimatePerSeason: unknown - low-traffic; likely under 20 parties per season based on obscurity relative to nearby Index-area classics

hazards: Steep, entirely off-trail approach through blowdown and brush, especially the first ~600 ft above the river
Cliff bands around 4,200-4,400 ft on the peak's north side that require careful route-finding to bypass
Exposed ~10 ft Class 5 mantle step at roughly 6,100 ft on the summit ridge — harder than the published Class 3 rating suggests
Permanent ice/snow patches on north and east aspects near the summit, present even in late summer
North Fork Skykomish River crossing can be hazardous during high water or early-season snowmelt
No reliable cell coverage anywhere on route
watch_out: The published 'Class 3' rating undersells two short sections that are genuinely Class 4-5 — don't commit to the ridge unprepared for a real 5th-class move
The 4,200-4,400 ft cliff bands can cliff you out if you traverse too high or low — locate the described bypass before committing to a line
This is one of the least-visited Everett-area peaks; don't count on other parties, a boot path, or cell signal for help if something goes wrong

weather.typical: Cascade summer alpine weather typical of the Index/Wild Sky Wilderness area - warm and mostly dry within the Jul-Sep window, but exposed timber and ridge terrain can hold moisture longer after a wet spell
weather.probability: Afternoon thunderstorms and sudden weather changes are possible in the Cascades during the summer window; an early start reduces exposure on the ridge if weather builds

seasonal_hazards.exposure: Route-finding in dense timber on the approach, plus real fall exposure on the exposed summit moves and loose rock along the minor gendarmes of the west ridge - a slip in either zone carries serious consequence

itinerary.cal: Snow often lingers in the approach gullies and on the ridge into late June/early July, so many parties carry an ice axe (and sometimes microspikes) for early-season ascents; by August the line is mostly dry talus and scrambling.

days.note: From the Barclay Lake trailhead, parties follow the maintained trail briefly before dropping into off-trail travel along Barclay Creek/Tailgunner Ravine, gaining the broad Tailgunner Pass/Gunn Basin area, then scramble the West Ridge to the summit. The whole outing is done car-to-car in a single long day; the crux is route-finding and steep brush/talus on the approach, not the ridge itself, which is class 2-3 scrambling with a short exposed step near the top.
days.title: Car-to-car: approach, West Ridge, summit, return

schedule.label: Leave Barclay Lake trailhead
schedule.detail: Start on the maintained Barclay Lake trail from the ~2,300 ft trailhead.

schedule.label: Leave the trail
schedule.detail: Cut off-trail up the Barclay Creek/Tailgunner Ravine drainage; steep brush and boulder-hopping.

schedule.label: Reach Tailgunner Pass / Gunn Basin
schedule.detail: Broad ~5,300-5,400 ft saddle; views open up onto the West Ridge line.

schedule.label: Start West Ridge scramble
schedule.detail: Class 2-3 terrain, with a short exposed step/headwall below the summit dome.

schedule.label: Summit (5,839 ft)
schedule.detail: Weather on this ridge can turn quickly; most parties don't linger long.

schedule.label: Back at trailhead
schedule.detail: Descend the same West Ridge line back into the basin, then retrace the approach.

days.objective: Summit Tailgunner Peak (5,839 ft) via the West Ridge

itinerary.totalNote: A single long day car-to-car: roughly 8-9 hours, ~3,200 ft gain over ~6.4 miles, most of it off-trail travel to Tailgunner Pass before a class 2-3 scramble up the West Ridge and back down the same line.
